endorsements.quote: The Utah safe harbor simply requires documentation of how these practices are implemented, including regular compliance audits.

unlisted_practices: Develop detailed and practical best practices for mental health generative AI, especially for consumer-facing use, and keep them current.
Move from risk-only analysis to risk-benefit analysis when evaluating mental health AI agents.
Develop new paradigms for pre-deployment safety testing, continuous monitoring, patient and provider education, and crisis escalation for mental health AI.
Policymakers and professional organizations should regularly revisit regulatory approaches to AI in mental health care as the field evolves.
Lay the regulatory foundation for mental health agents that are more engaging and beneficial to people with lived experience than general-purpose chatbots.
Policymakers should clarify whether mental health agents fall under FDA device regulation, state professional licensure, or consumer protection law.
Include people with lived experience, practitioners, academics, and companies in balanced stakeholder engagement when making mental health AI policy.
Provide psychiatrists with education and support to understand generative AI.

screen.reason: The article is a commentary/policy perspective summarizing findings from Utah's regulatory review of generative AI mental health agents to inform legislation, governance, and best-practice guidance.
